messages:
Simon: heads-up — prod-rt-03 hit an OOM at 10:12 while serving a ~15k token convo. KV cache memory climbed steadily and then a bunch of fragments were pinned. Host OOM killed the process.
Maria: ugh. did the kernel-switch logs show any unusual allocations?
Simon: attaching the short dump (stack and `/proc/meminfo` snippet). looks like many small KV slab allocations never recycled; eviction kept skipping them due to reuse_window logic.
Jess: can you paste the metric query for the mem spike? want to see correlation with batching changes rolled yesterday.
Simon: `sum(container_memory_usage_bytes) by (instance) |> rate(1m)` — spike starts at 10:05 and grows until 10:12. batching config change at 10:00 increased max_batch_tokens from 2048 -> 4096 on this pool.
Dennis: oh — that batch growth could increase per-request prefix retention time. more prefetched KV pages pinned longer.
Maria: hypothesis: larger batches extend KV reuse lifetime and increase fragmentation because small prefix slices aren't coalesced. eviction sees them as hot due to reuse_window and avoids evicting; net effect = pile-up.
Jess: agree. two quick mitigations we can flip from console: 1) revert max_batch_tokens to 2048, 2) lower reuse_window from 300s -> 60s for prod-rt-03 pool. both safe to roll back quickly.
Simon: also want to try a compaction cadence tweak: run background `kv_compact` pass every 120s instead of 10m for hosts serving long contexts. cheap but may reduce pinned fragment count.
Dennis: note: compaction increases CPU and could add jitter. maybe gate compaction on fragment_count > X so it only runs when needed.
Maria: proposed short playbook: 
- step 0: OpsBot annotate incident 
- step 1 (0-5m): revert batch size to 2048 and set reuse_window=60s on prod-rt-03 (owner: Jess) 
- step 2 (5-20m): enable thresholded compaction (fragment_count > 5000) with cadence=120s (owner: Dennis) 
- step 3 (20-60m): monitor telemetry for drop in pinned_fragments & mem usage; if not improved, trigger graceful degrade route to smaller model variant (owner: Simon) 
- step 4: collect heap profiles + kv slab histogram for postmortem (owner: Maria)

Jess: I'll revert batch size now and push reuse_window change. doing it as a canary on prod-rt-03a first.
OpsBot: runbook: applied config change `max_batch_tokens=2048` to prod-rt-03a (canary).
TelemetryBot: metric alert cleared on prod-rt-03a — memory trend stabilizing after canary change.
Simon: good sign. but we still need a durable fix: consider eviction hysteresis instead of absolute reuse_window — e.g., prefer evicting low-hit fragments older than max_age if free_mem < threshold. this avoids skipping evictions when memory is tight.
Maria: eviction hysteresis + compaction gating sounds promising. also add telemetry label `kv.reuse_hits` to better track which fragments are artificially kept hot by batching.
Jess: action items: I’ll finish canary rollback and open a PR with `reuse_window` paramization + `eviction_hysteresis` opt-in (w/ unit tests). Dennis — can you prototype thresholded compaction?
Dennis: on it. I'll also simulate long context sessions locally with synthetic requests to reproduce pinned fragment pattern (script will be in `eng-runtime/kv/tests/sim_longctx.sh`).
Simon: once PRs land, let's run a 2h soak on the canary pool and then rollout. also update the console alarm to trigger auto-fallback to smaller model variant when `kv.pinned_fragments` > 8000 for > 5m.
Maria: leaving a note for postmortem: correlate with yesterday's batching rollout and include kernel selection logs — if quant kernel switch coincided, that could have affected slab layout.
Jess: thanks team. I'll post PR links and canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:
